target_customer: Robotics researchers and humanoid-robot companies that need dexterous hands and human hand-manipulation data
problem: Humanoids lack hands dexterous enough for contact-rich manipulation; simple grippers fail on non-rigid objects and teleoperation does not scale or capture touch and pressure.
business_model: Hardware sales of dexterous robot hands (ProHand) plus a data-collection glove (ProGlove)
product_category: Robotics hardware: dexterous hands and tactile data capture

founders.name: Jay Li
prior_employers: Tesla (led electronics on the Optimus program)
founders.background_notes: TNW: founded Proception six days after leaving Tesla. Apple/Aurora/Aeva history is from a Dealroom news summary.

technical_complexity.rationale: A 22-degree-of-freedom tendon-driven hand with integrated tactile skin is hardware research-grade for a small team, requiring actuation, sensing and control integration.

defensibility.rationale: Hand design know-how and sensor skin are hard but contested: Tesla's lawsuit alleged similarity to its own designs, and Chinese makers ship far larger volumes (Linkerbot reportedly over 1,000 units a month, 2026).

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Tesla sued Proception and Jay Li in June 2025 over alleged confidential file downloads and similar hand designs, then dismissed the case in June 2026 after a settlement; Tesla still builds hands in-house. TNW (June 2026) says Linkerbot holds about 80% of the high-DoF hand market.

market_need_then: Humanoid robot makers were building their own hands because grippers and teleoperation were insufficient, and Tesla's Optimus program showed hands were a major engineering bottleneck, which created demand for dexterous hands and training data.

branding.domain_note: Uses proception.ai; domain history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Short, confident statements: 'Human-level dexterity.', 'Built Like a Machine. Works Like a Human.'

branding.brand_signature: Product naming system ProHand and ProGlove; tagline about threading a needle

brand_strength.rationale: Too early and no sources about the brand; press focused on the Tesla lawsuit and funding rather than the name.

outcome_analysis: Proception is an early-stage company that raised an $11M seed led by First Round in June 2026, shortly after settling a year-long Tesla trade-secret suit and starting to ship its first ProHand units. Founder-market fit is strong, since the CEO led electronics on Optimus, and humanoid robotics funding gave a tailwind. Risks are the Tesla legacy, hardware execution, and low-cost Chinese hand makers that already ship at scale; it is too early to call an outcome.
notes: Dealroom (aggregator) lists a $125K YC investment in March 2025 and a $44M valuation for the seed; neither is confirmed elsewhere and neither is recorded as a round. Competitors at founding: no sources dated near W25 were found (search results were mostly 2026), so the list is empty; Linkerbot, Genesis AI and Xynova are 2026-era players mentioned in outcome_analysis context only. The YC page lists founded 2024 while TNW says Li left Tesla and founded the company shortly before the 2025 lawsuit. Web Archive skipped.
